differences.upstreamObservation: The pinned upstream Dogwood 1.1.2 value model has no ipaddr or datetime variant, so a typed ipaddr or datetime context value cannot reach the upstream authorizer as a typed value. The upstream comparison of that context attribute against the policy literal is therefore false and the upstream decision is a clean Deny with no error, no determining rule and no policy error.
differences.d3Observation: D3 evaluates the same typed context value through CedarSharp, which models the ipaddr and datetime Cedar extension types. The comparison against the policy literal is true and the D3 decision is a clean Allow that names the single determining permit rule, with no error and no policy error.
differences.basis: Owner decision for commission DOGWOOD-SHARP-D3-IMPL-01-R4 (C-23 compatibility ceiling closure). The limitation is pinned to the upstream Dogwood 1.1.2 value model: dogwood-language/src/interpreter/value.rs declares the Value enum without an ipaddr or datetime variant, and dogwood-language/src/api.rs documents the ip, datetime and duration extension values as unmodeled and carried as a raw __extn value. Upstream therefore cannot represent a typed ipaddr or datetime context value at all, while D3 evaluates it with the CedarSharp engine. This row approves the representability ceiling for exactly the two C-23 cases listed above. It is not a general permission to disagree on authorization outcomes: it does not cover any other case, any other observation, or any difference in the stage, operation-failed state, error categories or policy error IDs, and the harness rejects a case whose observed difference reaches outside the authorizedDifferenceFields scope below.
differences.failClosedEffect: The upstream side denies and the D3 side allows only for a caller-supplied typed ipaddr or datetime context value that the upstream value model cannot represent. Every other observation of these two cases still matches exactly: both sides reach the evaluation stage, neither side reports an operation failure, neither side reports an error or an error category, neither side reports a policy error, and the determining set matches except for the single permit rule the D3 side attributes. A typed value that does not equal the policy literal is denied by D3, and an invalid or malformed typed value fails closed on the D3 side.
